name: State of Texas
policy_note: Structural research pointer only. NO substantive statutory rules — student packets are facts-only; finding the controlling law is the exercise. Code-level locators are navigational aids. Instructor notes may cite specifics, verified at publish.

district_court.name: Texas District Court
district_court.note: Trial court of general jurisdiction (higher-value civil, felony criminal, family, and land-title disputes).

county_courts_at_law.name: Texas County Courts at Law / Constitutional County Courts
county_courts_at_law.note: Limited and probate jurisdiction; some counties have statutory Probate Courts.

intermediate_appellate.name: Texas Court of Appeals
intermediate_appellate.note: Intermediate appellate courts, organized into 14 districts.

highest_courts.note: Texas has a bifurcated high court.
highest_courts.civil: Supreme Court of Texas (highest court for civil and juvenile matters)
highest_courts.criminal: Texas Court of Criminal Appeals (highest court for criminal matters)

real_estate_conventions.note: The m14 shape is a Texas real-estate purchase negotiation. Instruments affecting title are recorded with the County Clerk of the county where the land lies; acknowledgment before a Texas notary public is required for recording. Texas is a notice jurisdiction. Students research the current conveyancing and title framework themselves.
real_estate_conventions.notary: Texas Notary Public, commissioned by the Secretary of State; acknowledgment required for recordable instruments.
common_documents: General Warranty Deed or Special Warranty Deed
Deed of Trust (Texas uses deeds of trust, not mortgages)

navigational_code_areas: Conveyances, recording, and title: Tex. Prop. Code (Title 2 Conveyances; Title 3 Public Records) — a starting point for m14.
Real-estate contracts and the statute of frauds appear in the Tex. Bus. & Com. Code — a starting point for m14.

disclaimer: Structural/navigational reference only, current as of 2026. Verify all law against the official sources above; nothing here is legal advice.
